newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares jump, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares jump, seen extending gains.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday jumped after Tuesday's fall and analysts said the higher turnover and low number of orders signalled more growth on Thursday as large investors were apparently returning after recent falls.
"Today's large turnover and low number of orders suggests large investors are entering and that the market should continue rising," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

Large-cap, fundamentally sound firms such as industrial and trading conglomerate Elektrim have seen large turnovers over the past few sessions, with Elektrim surging 9.9 percent in Wednesday's high turnover.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 3.1 percent to 13,891.6 points and turnover jumped 54.1 percent to 119.4 million zlotys ($42.4 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 66 to eight with six stocks flat.
The WIG fell 14.6 percent over the final two thirds of October before rebounding last week.
Analysts said the news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin emerged well from his heart operation and that the U.S. presidential and congressional elections maintained the status quo may have helped.
Analysts said investors might expect the Polish Senate next week to reject the lower house's tax cut for low earners, seen as raising the budget deficit and spurring inflation.
Analysts said the market might not be hurt by Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko's threat on Wednesday to quit if the lower house's tax rates are kept.
Analysts said loss leader construction firm Espebepe, down 5.7 percent, fell after a speculative gain on the back of a several-session plunge on a bankruptcy threat.
NFI units rose 2.2 percent to 142.5 zlotys ($50.6) and rose 1.8 percent in continuous trade, where stock turnover was at 3.8 million zlotys ($1.3 million).
